validity.recommendation: no action on existence — well documented
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE strongly confirmed by primary federal records, independent of any Enbridge/GEM material. Federal Register notice 61 FR 41601 (1996-08-09, Docket Nos. CP96-678-000/CP96-679-000) recites that 'by order issued May 16, 1996, in Docket No. CP96-307-000, the Commission granted [Shell Gas Pipeline Company] authority to construct and operate a 30-inch diameter natural gas pipeline ... extending approximately 50 miles from the "A" Platform in Garden Banks Block 128, offshore Louisiana, to the "P" Platform in South Marsh Island 76, offshore Louisiana,' with Garden Banks Gas Pipeline, LLC (GBGP) as successor-in-interest (members: Shell Enchilada Gas Pipeline Co. 80%, Hess Garden Banks Gas Gathering Inc. 20% at inception). Two further Federal Register/govinfo.gov FERC tariff notices (Docket GT98-44-000, filed 1998-05-21, and Docket RP99-5-000, filed 1998-10-01) confirm GBGP was an active tariff-filing FERC entity through 1998, the first covering an imbalance-revenue-crediting reporting period of Oct 1, 1996-Sep 30, 1997. Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_Banks_Pipeline), Enbridge's own 2020 asset factsheet PDF, an archived 2008 Enbridge offshore-systems table (web.archive.org/web/20081011120659), and an Oct 2024 Enbridge press release (new bp Canyon Gathering System tying into 'Enbridge's downstream FERC-regulated Garden Banks Gas Pipeline') all independently corroborate the line is real, current, and still in the Enbridge offshore portfolio as of 2024. Reuters and rigzone.com pieces cited on the wiki page are dead/bot-walled with no Wayback capture (see notes on those units) but are not needed for existence — the FERC record plus Wikipedia/Enbridge/press chain is more than sufficient. Not a phantom, not GEM-only. Opened 12 of the wiki page's harvested citations' targets in some form (7 harvested + 5 more found independently); 2 (rigzone.com, reuters.com) could not be reached live or via Wayback — see per-unit notes.

GEM's current PipelineType = 'gathering'. Every independent source that classifies this line at all calls it a TRANSMISSION pipeline, not a gathering line: Wikipedia states outright 'The Garden Banks Pipeline is a 30-inch diameter natural gas transmission pipeline'; Enbridge's own 2020 factsheet section header 'Garden Banks Pipeline' states 'The Garden Banks Pipeline is a 30-inch-diameter, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)-regulated offshore natural gas transmission pipeline' and lists 'Nature of asset: Offshore natural gas transmission pipeline'; the Oct 2024 Enbridge press release calls it 'Enbridge's downstream FERC-regulated Garden Banks Gas Pipeline'. The 2008 Enbridge offshore-gt.com corridor table is itself the clearest internal evidence of the distinction GEM's vocab is trying to capture: within the same 'Garden Banks Corridor' it lists 'Garden Banks Pipeline' (50 mi, 1000 MMcf/d, Regulating Agency = FERC, i.e. transmission-grade jurisdictional pipeline) as a SEPARATE line item from 'Magnolia Gathering Lateral' (50 mi, 250 MMcf/d, Regulating Agency = MMS, i.e. the actual gathering asset in the same corridor). So Enbridge's own operational taxonomy treats Garden Banks Pipeline itself as the FERC-jurisdictional transmission line and reserves 'gathering' for the separate Magnolia lateral. GEM's controlled vocab (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md) allows both 'transmission' and 'gathering' as PipelineType values, so this is a real classification error to fix, not a vocab gap.

validity.recommendation: correct LengthKnown from 84.00 km to ~80 km (50 miles) — pending Baird confirmation
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown = 84.00 km. Every source found states the pipeline is 50 MILES long, which converts to 80.47 km, not 84 km — a ~4.2% / 3.5 km disagreement. This is stated identically and independently by: (1) the original 1996 FERC certificate record (Federal Register 61 FR 41601, reciting the Commission's May 16, 1996 order: 'approximately 50 miles from the "A" Platform in Garden Banks Block 128 ... to the "P" Platform in South Marsh Island 76') — a government regulatory record wholly independent of Enbridge; (2) Enbridge's own 2020 asset factsheet ('Length: 50 miles (80 km)'); (3) the archived 2008 Enbridge offshore-gt.com corridor table ('Garden Banks Pipeline 50 [mi]'); (4) Wikipedia ('it spans for 50 miles (80 kilometres)'). No source found supports 84 km specifically. This is a material spec disagreement, not a rounding artifact (84 km ≠ 50 mi under any standard conversion). Did NOT stage a Length [ref] fill supporting the current 84.00 km value because no independent source corroborates it — flagging as a concern instead, per standing spec-verification rule. Recommend Baird review and correct to 80 km / 50 mi if independently agreed, rather than the agent silently overwriting a value column.

cross_row_leads.facts: Roster lists P0294 as 'Magnolia Intrastate Pipeline' (route ?->Mississippi). This 2008 Enbridge table shows a distinct offshore 'Magnolia Gathering Lateral' (50 mi, 250 MMcf/d, MMS-regulated, Enbridge 100%) in the same 'Garden Banks Corridor' as P0192, feeding the Magnolia platform/field — and Enbridge's Oct 2024 press release refers to an 'existing Magnolia Gas Gathering Pipeline' that the new bp Canyon Gathering System will tie into upstream of Garden Banks. Whoever works P0294 should check whether that row is this same offshore Magnolia lateral (in which case its Mississippi/onshore termini in GEM may be wrong or it may be a distinct segment), or a genuinely separate onshore Mississippi intrastate system unrelated to the Garden Banks corridor. Not resolved here — flagged only.

Same 2008 Enbridge table lists 'Mississippi Canyon Pipeline 45 [mi] 800 [MMcf/d] FERC Enbridge 100% Enbridge' under the 'Mississippi Canyon Corridor.' Roster shows P0217 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline' with len=44.5 km and cap=800.00 — capacity matches exactly, but 45 MILES = ~72.4 km, not 44.5 km, a similar mile-vs-km-shaped discrepancy to the one found on this row (P0192, 50 mi vs GEM's 84 km). Worth a targeted re-check when P0217 is swept — same pattern, different direction of error, possibly worth checking whether GEM's LengthKnown fields across this Enbridge-offshore-pipeline family were derived from a units mix-up rather than mile-to-km conversion.

summary: P0192 Garden Banks Gas Pipeline exists and is well-documented (1996 FERC certificate record + Wikipedia + Enbridge factsheet/press through 2024); staged REFS_ADDED fills for Status/Fuel/Capacity/Diameter/FuelSource/Owner/Operator plus a Location fill correcting the non-state 'Gulf of Mexico' StartState/EndState to Louisiana, and a medium-tier Start/Construction-year fill (1996/1997); filed 2 concerns — classification (PipelineType should be 'transmission' not 'gathering', per Wikipedia + Enbridge's own factsheet/press language) and spec (LengthKnown=84.00 km is unsupported; every source says 50 mi/~80 km) — plus a duplicate check that clears P0192 itself but raises cross-row leads for P0294 (Magnolia) and P0217 (Mississippi Canyon, same mile/km-shaped length discrepancy).
